# Pressing leaves

A made-up article for the compiler's tests: how to press a leaf flat, in three short sections, with a note and a table.

## Gathering

Pick leaves on a dry afternoon, when the dew has gone.[^herbarium] Choose ones with no holes, and ==keep each flat== between two sheets of paper on the way home.

> [!tip] Carry a book
> An old paperback makes a good press for the walk back.

- Maple turns red in autumn.
- Fern keeps its green.
- Ginkgo goes a clear yellow.

## Pressing

Lay each leaf between blotting sheets, then stack heavy books on top. A press needs about $m \geq 5$ kilograms.

| Leaf | Days | Weight (kg) |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Maple | 7 | 5 |
| Fern | 10 | 6 |
| Ginkgo | 5 | 4 |

> [!note]- More about blotting paper
> Change the sheets after two days, so the leaves dry and do not mould.

### Drying

> Patience is the whole method.

Leave the stack alone. A site template would read `{{ .Title }}` and `{% raw %}` as code, so the compiler writes them as text.

## Keeping

Glue the dry leaves into a notebook. For the next step, go back to [[#Gathering]] or [the top](#pressing-leaves), or try [[compile-kinds.booklet]]. A [museum's own guide](https://example.org/museum) goes further.

[^herbarium]: *The Pocket Herbarium*, 3rd edition (2020), p. 41: "Gather on a dry day." Verified 2026-10-01.
